This code updates earlier work analyzing GDP by county in Maryland.
It is examining the Bureau of Economic Analysis Real GDP by County for 2024 and earlier years.
https://apps.bea.gov/iTable/?reqid=70&step=30&isuri=1&year_end=-1&classification=naics&state=0&yearbegin=-1&unit_of_measure=percentchange&major_area=0&area=04000&year=-1&tableid=512&category=1512&area_type=0&statistic=1&selected_income_data=0#



```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
#install.packages("formattable")
library(formattable)
library(janitor)
```


#Bureau of Economic Research Local GDP data
```{r}
bea2024 <- read_csv("./data/bea_md_gdp_county_2024_CAGDP9.csv", skip=3) |> 
  clean_names()

bea2019 <-read_csv("./data/bea_md_gdp_county_2019_CAGDP9.csv", skip=3) |> 
  clean_names()

bea2014 <- read_csv("./data/bea_md_gdp_county_2014_CAGDP9.csv", skip=3) |> 
  clean_names()

```


# Examine description.
Documentation
CAGDP9 Real GDP by county 1
(thousands of chained 2017 dollars)

Chained dollars are inflation adjusted since 2017 and that strips out the effects of inflation over time.

Chained-dollar values. Chained-dollar values are calculated by multiplying the quantity index by the current-dollar value in the reference year (2017) and then dividing by 100. Percent changes calculated from real quantity indexes and chained-dollar levels are conceptually the same; any differences are due to rounding. **Chained-dollar values are not additive,** because the relative weights for a given period differ from those of the reference year. In tables that display chained-dollar values, a "residual" line shows the difference between the sum of detailed chained-dollar series and its corresponding aggregate.
https://www.bea.gov/news/gdp-release-additional-information



1. Real GDP is in thousands of chained 2017 dollars. Industry detail is based on the 2017 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS).
2. The private goods-producing industries consist of agriculture, forestry, fishing, and hunting; mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction; construction; and manufacturing.
3. The private services-producing industries consist of utilities; wholesale trade; retail trade; transportation and warehousing, excluding Postal Service; information; finance and insurance; real estate, rental, and leasing; professional, scientific, and technical services; management of companies; administrative and support and waste management and remediation services; educational services; health care and social assistance; arts, entertainment, and recreation; accommodation and food services; and other services (except government and government enterprises).
Last updated: February 5, 2026-- new statistics for 2024; revised statistics for 2020-2023.
Suggested citation: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, "CAGDP9 Real GDP by county 1" (accessed Monday, November 2, 2026). 

#Filter just for total, private, government industries

```{r}
bea2024_govt <- bea2024 |> 
  filter(line_code %in% c(1, 2, 83)) |> 
  subset(select = -c(line_code)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = description, values_from = x2024) |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  rename(government_24 = government_and_government_enterprises, total_24 = all_industry_total, private_24 = private_industries) |> 
  mutate(across(c(total_24, private_24, government_24), as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(geo_name = str_remove_all(geo_name, ", MD"))

```


# Same but for 2019 and 2014
Filter just for total, private, government industries

```{r}
bea2019_govt <- bea2019 |> 
  filter(line_code %in% c(1, 2, 83)) |> 
  subset(select = -c(line_code)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = description, values_from = x2019) |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  rename(government_19 = government_and_government_enterprises, total_19 = all_industry_total, private_19 = private_industries) |> 
  mutate(across(c(total_19, private_19, government_19), as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(geo_name = str_remove_all(geo_name, ", MD"))


bea2014_govt <- bea2014 |> 
  filter(line_code %in% c(1, 2, 83)) |> 
  subset(select = -c(line_code)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = description, values_from = x2014) |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  rename(government_14 = government_and_government_enterprises, total_14 = all_industry_total, private_14 = private_industries) |> 
  mutate(across(c(total_14, private_14, government_14), as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(geo_name = str_remove_all(geo_name, ", MD"))
```

#Join all three

```{r}

bea_all <- bea2024_govt |> 
  inner_join(bea2019_govt, by=c("geo_name", "geo_fips")) |> 
  inner_join(bea2014_govt, by=c("geo_name", "geo_fips"))  |> 
  select(geo_name, total_24, total_19, total_14, government_24, government_19, government_14, private_24, private_19, private_14, geo_fips)
             
```

# Plot the pct
```{r}
ggplot(bea2024_govt, aes(x = pct_gov, y = reorder(geo_name, pct_gov), fill = pct_gov)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Pct government in local Maryland counties",
    subtitle = "2024 BEA data",
    caption = "Graphic by Rob Wells, 10-26-2026",
    y = "county",
    x = "Pct govt of GDP"
  )

```

Adding labels, thanks Gemimi
```{r}
ggplot(bea2024_govt, aes(x = pct_gov, y = reorder(geo_name, pct_gov), fill = geo_name == "Maryland")) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  # Set colors: gold/yellow for Maryland (TRUE), grey for everything else (FALSE)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#FFD700", "FALSE" = "grey75")) +
  
  # Add labels to the bars
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(pct_gov, 1), "%")),
    hjust = -0.2,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +
  
  # Expand x-axis slightly so outside labels aren't cut off
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Pct government in local Maryland counties",
    subtitle = "2024 BEA data",
    caption = "Graphic by Rob Wells, 10-26-2026",
    y = "county",
    x = "Pct govt of GDP"
  )
```

#Filter for both above-median census_response_rate2020 and Percent of membership in Civic Organization.

```{r}
# above <- pg |> 
#   filter(census_response_rate2020 >= 0.7190 & pct_anymembershp_zip >=  0.5037) |> 
#   arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))

above <- pg |> 
  filter(census_response_rate2020 > median(census_response_rate2020, na.rm = TRUE) & 
         pct_anymembershp_zip > median(pct_anymembershp_zip, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))



summary(above$census_response_rate2020)
 #  Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
 # 0.7210  0.7535  0.8010  0.8027  0.8500  0.9000 

summary(above$pct_anymembershp_zip)
 #   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
 # 0.5058  0.5230  0.5475  0.5656  0.6007  0.6523
```

#Tracts with below median per capita income and higher than median participation
```{r}

low_and_active <- pg |> 
  filter(income_per_capita < 32613 & pct_anymembershp_zip >  0.5037) |> 
  arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))

write_csv(low_and_active, "./output/pg_co_low_income_active.csv")

```
